item.title: 'The Dog Stars' Review: Jacob Elordi fights for survival in Ridley Scott's dull post-apocalyptic western
item.description: Fox News Digital reviews 20th Century Studios' "The Dog Stars" starring Jacob Elordi, Josh Brolin, Margaret Qualley, Guy Pearce and Allison Janney. Directed by Ridley Scott.
item.content:encoded:
Ridley Scott has directed some of Hollywood's most iconic movies, from "Alien" and "Blade Runner" to "Thelma & Louise" and "Gladiator." But over the past decade, his films have mostly ranged from OK to meh. 

Unfortunately, his latest falls in the latter category. 

"The Dog Stars," adapted from Peter Heller's 2012 novel, follows Hig (Jacob Elordi), a mechanic trying to navigate a post-apocalyptic America that had been ravaged by a deadly flu years earlier. He has taken shelter at an abandoned Colorado airport and is joined by Bangley (Josh Brolin), a brutish former Marine with great aim, and Hig's Belgian shepherd, Jasper. 

‘MUTINY’ REVIEW: JASON STATHAM TAKES NO PRISONERS IN MINDLESS BUT AMUSING BRAWLER FLICK ON THE HIGH SEAS

The routine is as follows: Hig flies into Denver in his little yellow plane to seek supplies, stops by his old house, triggering flashbacks of his late wife, occasionally makes deliveries to a rural community of Mennonite farmers, and sometimes joins Bangley in killing trespassers who may be infected with the virus before burning their bodies as a precaution.

Hig thinks there is more civilization beyond the mountains, namely in Grand Junction. Bangley thinks it's a fool's errand and that leaving Eric would certainly lead to death. But Hig can't deny his own convictions, so he ultimately decides to seek life elsewhere. 

‘THE END OF OAK STREET’ REVIEW: ANNE HATHAWAY, EWAN MCGREGOR FIGHT DINOSAURS IN SURPRISINGLY FUN MOVIE

He'll come across some interesting characters on his journey, like the boorish rancher Jack and his daughter Cima (Guy Pearce and Margaret Qualley) and the eccentric Darlene (Allison Janney). There's also what's been dubbed the "Reapers," a group of tatted savages who will kill and destroy anything in their path. 

The cast does a fine job. Elordi, the Australian up-and-comer known for his breakout role in HBO's "Euphoria" and appearing more recently in "Wuthering Heights" and Netflix's "Frankenstein" (which earned him his first Oscar nomination), is flexing his leading man muscles. Both Brolin and Pearce earn a few laughs for their rough-around-the-edges performances. And Janney elevates any project she's in, regardless how zany her character is. 

'TONY' REVIEW: ANTHONY BOURDAIN'S COMING-OF-AGE STORY UNFOLDS IN CHARMING DRAMEDY

However, I never felt strongly invested as a viewer. Except for a few gun battles, "The Dog Stars" was fairly dull. Despite Elordi's best efforts, Hig is a run-of-the-mill dystopian protagonist, so there isn't much to work with (perhaps the source material is to blame). 

The guitar-forward score from Harry Gregson-Williams only furthers the film's sleepy western vibe. At least all the mountain scenery was pleasant to look at.

‘SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY’ REVIEW: TOM HOLLAND, ZENDAYA RETURN FOR ACTION-PACKED, EMOTIONAL SEQUEL

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Ridley Scott's "The Dog Stars" is the latest installment in the prolific director's middling stretch of films that will likely leave the mind shortly after viewing. And when that happens, you question why the movie was made to begin with.

"The Dog Stars" is rated R for strong violence and language. Running time: 1 hour, 58 minutes. In theaters now.

item.title: Hilaria Baldwin explains how she stays fit raising 7 kids with ‘bathroom workouts’ and an unexpected diet
item.description: Hilaria Baldwin shares her fitness routine, which includes bathroom workouts, while raising seven kids and pokes fun at Alec Baldwin for not being able to touch his toes.
item.content:encoded:
Hilaria Baldwin is taking the phrase "squeeze in a workout" to a whole new level.

The 42-year-old "Nation's Dumbest" contestant and mother of seven told Fox News Digital her fitness routine doesn’t always happen in a gym — or even in a dedicated workout space. Sometimes, it happens right there in the bathroom.

"I run every day… I found being a mom, if I can get 30 minutes of my cardio, it helps my mind... It gets me like sort of a little bit more regulated with my nervous system, so I really like that," she shared when asked about her go-to workout with a hectic schedule.

HILARIA BALDWIN SHARES MARRIAGE LESSON SHE TELLS FRIENDS AFTER SURVIVING 'UPS AND OUR DOWNS' WITH ALEC BALDWIN

"Then I obviously do my yoga, my little bathroom workouts, or just like a stop-and-drop little workout. I love Physique 57. Any kind of barre classes I think are really great."

And Hilaria isn’t just talking about quick bathroom sweat sessions.

Last month, she gave her fans a front-row look at exactly what those workouts can look like, showing off her physique in a bikini while demonstrating glute exercises in a bathroom.

HILARIA BALDWIN FLAUNTS FIT FIGURE IN BIKINI AS FANS MARVEL AT MOM OF 7

Despite her fitness-focused lifestyle, Hilaria insisted she isn't living exclusively on lettuce.

"It's not always the same," Hilaria said when asked what a typical day of meals looks like. 

"I think people think that I just eat salad all the time, which I’ve definitely done that in the past. But the other day — the baby of the family, we opened up pints of ice cream, two different pints of ice cream at 9 PM. So, sometimes it looks like that."

WATCH: HILARIA BALDWIN SQUEEZES IN ‘BATHROOM WORKOUTS’ AS A MOM OF 7

She added, "Eat good things and then enjoy. Have the slice of pizza once in a while. Have the ice cream. I think it’s just a bit of a balance."

When Fox News Digital asked if her husband, Alec Baldwin, ever joins her workouts, she laughed and said he’s not the most flexible person.

"Can’t touch his toes. I literally married the most inflexible person I have ever met."

'PERFECT' WORKOUT FORMULA CAN TAKE JUST 10 MINUTES A DAY, HILARIA BALDWIN SAYS

After more than 15 years together, seven children and plenty of public scrutiny, Hilaria shared the relationship advice she said has helped keep her longtime relationship strong.

"Oh, it’s been more than 15 years. We met February 2011. You both have to want to be there," she told Fox News Digital.

WATCH: HILARIA BALDWIN REVEALS WHAT KEPT MARRIAGE TO ALEC BALDWIN STRONG THROUGH 'UPS AND DOWNS'

"Whenever my friends are coming to me, and they’re like it’s a new relationship, or they’re having a bump in it, I say, ‘if both people don’t really want to be there through your difficult moments, through your best moments, then it’s just not going to probably work out,’" the TV personality explained.

"Both Alec and I, through our ups and our downs and our sideways, we’ve wanted to be there. And I think that that’s what’s kept us strong."

Hilaria's candid comments come as she appears on FOX's celebrity competition series, "Nation's Dumbest."

WATCH: HILARIA BALDWIN PUSHES BACK ON BIGGEST MISCONCEPTION ABOUT HER

The show flips the traditional celebrity competition formula on its head: contestants aren't fighting to prove they're the smartest in the room. They're trying desperately to avoid being crowned the dumbest.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Hilaria joins an eclectic cast that includes Carmen Electra, Anthony Michael Hall, Ice-T, Elle King, Matt Leinart, Dr. Drew Pinsky, Steve-O, JoJo Siwa, Andrew Yang, Jon Heder and Chase Hudson.

At home, Hilaria and Alec have their own seven-member Baldwin brood: daughters Carmen, María and Ilaria, and sons Rafael, Leonardo, Romeo and Eduardo.

Alec is also the father of daughter Ireland Baldwin, whom he shares with ex-wife Kim Basinger. Ireland became a mother herself in 2023 when she welcomed daughter Holland, making Alec a first-time grandfather.

item.title: Stunned couple unearths 150-pound mystery hidden beneath their backyard for decades
item.description: A San Francisco couple unearthed a remarkable 150-pound limestone sculpture in their Russian Hill backyard, sparking a mystery with possible ties to artist Ralph Stackpole.
item.content:encoded:
A couple in San Francisco recently unearthed a 150-pound limestone sculpture buried in their backyard — setting off a search to uncover who created it and how it got there.

Greg Gatwood was doing yard work at the couple's Russian Hill home in May when he came across what he initially thought was a piece of concrete buried in the ground as his partner Judy Gittelsohn stood nearby.

Gatwood told Fox News Digital he tried to pry the object loose with a shovel before grabbing a pickaxe — and then spotted what appeared to be lips and a nose "peering" back at him.

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MYSTERIOUS FACE HIDDEN FOR CENTURIES IN BOOK OF REVELATION CITY

"I thought, well, maybe I should just break it into smaller pieces," Gatwood said. "Then I realized it was a statue.

"It was like something you see in a movie, almost cinematic, you know — a big beautiful statue like this."

Gittelsohn said she was stunned when Gatwood showed her the enormous, two-foot-wide statue — and was impressed by the quality of its craftsmanship.

"I was just shocked," she said. "What an enormous find."

ARCHAEOLOGISTS UNCOVER MASSIVE ARTIFACT DEPICTING PHARAOH THOUGHT TO HAVE CHALLENGED MOSES IN EXODUS

She added, "I was surprised. I was just gobsmacked."

Three months after their discovery, the couple is still searching for answers.

Gittelsohn, a professional artist, said she researched the sculpture. She believes it dates to the 1930s and may be connected to artists working under the Works Progress Administration (WPA).

The couple's home is near the former San Francisco Art Institute, where prominent sculptor Ralph Stackpole taught for decades — leading Gittelsohn to believe the piece may have a connection to him or one of his students.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

One clue supporting that theory, she said, is that the sculpture was carved from relatively inexpensive limestone rather than costlier materials such as marble or granite.

Gatwood believes the statue may have been used as garden art and that it was eventually buried with time.

"It's quite possible this statue was displayed in the garden and not so much buried, but just lost," he said.

After the couple received local attention for their find, Gittelsohn said a 93-year-old woman took an Uber to their home with her walker and knocked on their door.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The woman — one of several people who have reached out to the couple since the discovery became public — told them she had previously held a show featuring Ralph Stackpole's work. 

In September, the couple plans to put the sculpture on public display at the American Messenger Gallery in hopes that someone may recognize the piece or know who created it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"We think someone will eventually recognize it," Gatwood said.

The story comes about a year after a New Orleans couple made a similarly mysterious discovery in their backyard.

At the time, Daniella Santoro and Aaron Lorenz unearthed an ancient Roman funerary artifact that had been missing from an Italian museum for decades.

item.title: Kyle Busch's final words about Daytona come with a sobering Dale Earnhardt twist
item.description: The Coke Zero Sugar 400 marks the first NASCAR Cup Series race at Daytona International Speedway since Kyle Busch's stunning death back in May.
item.content:encoded:
It doesn't take long to spot a Kyle Busch fan at Daytona International Speedway.

In fact, drive under the tunnel and into the infield, and a "Rowdy Forever" banner is the first thing that greets you. It's not the only one. Not even close.

They're everywhere this weekend. Of course, that's expected.

This is the first NASCAR Cup Series race at Daytona since Busch's stunning death in May. The Coke Zero Sugar 400 is set to close the regular season later tonight — a little over three months since the sport lost its modern day Dale Earnhardt.

For better and for worse, those two will forever be attached at the hip.

KYLE BUSCH'S CHILLING MESSAGE AFTER FINAL NASCAR WIN A PAINFUL ENDING FOR MOURNING FANS

Busch's death in May was the first major NASCAR death for an active driver since Earnhardt died on the final turn of the 2001 Daytona 500.

For decades, Daytona gave Dale fits. He could win all the races, except the race.

Busch won just once at Daytona during his two decades in a Cup car, and never won a 500. It was the crown jewel he never got.

Lord knows he tried. Came close a couple times, too. Earlier this year, Busch grabbed his first Daytona 500 pole. He led 19 laps, but he fizzled late.

No, Kyle never loved Daytona the way Dale Earnhardt did. But he appreciated it. He respected it.

During February's 500, he led the third lap of the race, which was dedicated to Dale Earnhardt on what was the 25th anniversary of his death.

"Led lap 3 for Dale plus a few more today," he posted days after the race. "Made it to the end, just not in the right spot."

Now, the series returns for the first time since his death — and for the first time without an Earnhardt or a Busch in the field since 1978.

Yep. That's right. Saturday night's race will be the first Cup race at Daytona without an Earnhardt or a Busch in the field in 48 years. February 19, 1978.

For those who don't remember, Bobby Allison won that Daytona 500. Earnhardt would make his first Daytona start months later in the Firecracker 400.

Incredible. Forty-eight years. Nearly five decades!

So, yes, this sport has Earnhardt and Busch in its blood. Dale died in the '01 Daytona 500, which was Kurt Busch's first race. Kyle came into the series five years later as a rookie with Hendrick Motorsports.

UNEARTHED FAN VIDEO SHOWS WHO KYLE BUSCH REALLY WAS, NASCAR'S DARKEST HOUR & BUBBA WALLACE'S 'ROWDY' STORY

He'd go on to win 63 Cup races over the next two decades, including a pair of championships. He had 234 wins across all three NASCAR national series.

Busch won one Coca-Cola 600, two Southern 500s, and three Indianapolis 500 victories. He won once official race at Daytona, but did win a couple duels and the one Busch Clash on the road course back in 2021.

But Kyle never scored that elusive 500.

"Yeah, it’s a box we got to check," he said earlier this year. "Here we are. This is an opportunity to be able to do that. I’ve come down here a lot of years."

Daytona was never great to Kyle. It wasn't his favorite place to race. He didn't have the best luck.

But coming back here this weekend, it's clear this place misses him.

And like Dale, he's still everywhere you look.

item.title: WWE NXT Heatwave 2026 match card, preview and predictions
item.description: WWE NXT Heatwave features Zilla Fatu's first singles match in a fatal four-way NXT Championship bout at the Bert Ogden Arena in Edinburg, Texas.
item.content:encoded:
WWE NXT Heatwave will cap a wild day of professional wrestling on Sunday.

Four championship matches and a submission match will be featured on the card as Heatwave takes place at the Bert Ogden Arena in Edinburg, Texas.

The event marks the first singles match for newcomer Zilla Fatu, who burst onto the NXT scene earlier this month. Fatu immediately went after NXT champion Tony D’Angelo and was thrust into a fatal four-way match with the title on the line.

It’s one of the marquee matches on the card. Read below for the full card, a preview and predictions.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

==

It’s a rising star versus a legend. Nattie challenged Jaida Parker to a submission match for Heatwave as their rivalry turned up a notch. Parker will have a chance to prove to Nattie and the rest of the WWE Universe that she is who she says she is. Nattie gets a chance to continue to show why she’s the "lowkey legend" who continuously changes the game in the sport.

Prediction: Parker pulls out all the stops.

==

It’s going to be a long night for Myles Borne as he deals with the Vanity Project. First, he teams up with Tavion Heights to go up against Brad Baylor and Ricky Smokes. Borne and Heights have only held the tag titles for three weeks after winning it against Baylor and Smokes earlier this month.

Prediction: Borne and Heights hang on to win the tag titles.

==

It won’t be long before Borne is in another match with another Vanity Project member. Jackson Drake is looking for his shot at NXT gold in this North American Championship match. Drake beat Shiloh Hill with the help of Naraku to earn the chance at the title. Brad Baylor and Ricky Smokes may be unable to take down Borne, but it could end up being Drake’s night.

Prediction: Jackson Drake captures the title

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

==

NXT is unifying the Women’s North American Championship and the WWE Women’s Speed Championship. But there’s one wildcard – Kali Armstrong. The former Evolve women’s champion gets her first shot at gold. It will be an uphill battle as Zaria is a worthy champion and Sinclair has proven much in the ring over the last year. Will two reigns come to an end?

Prediction: Kali Armstrong has herself a night

==

Kendal Grey and Kelani Jordan could both be on the main roster right now and be able to swim with the sharks. For now, the NXT Women’s Championship is on the line as Grey goes up against Jordan. Grey has a rocket strapped to her back since she came over from Evolve. Jordan has complained about not getting proper opportunities in NXT as of late. Jordan has a slight advantage since Grey is coming into the match with an ear injury. Jordan is smart enough to use that to her advantage in this one.

Prediction: Grey wins this one in a hard-fought battle.

==

Old NXT, new NXT, a newcomer, an old face – it doesn’t matter. Tony D’Angelo has knocked everyone down since he returned to NXT programming. He now leads the men’s division as the champion but has a huge task in front of him. Grayson Waller is as hungry as ever. Cruz Montana has momentum on his side. Zilla Fatu is looking to make history. D’Angelo has held the NXT Championship for nearly 150 days. He’s the longest reigning champion since Oba Femi in 2025. Could WWE fans see an upset to end Heatwave?

Prediction: Zilla Fatu wins the title in his first singles match on NXT.

==

WWE NXT Heatwave begins at 3 p.m. ET and can be seen on the CW Network in the United States.

item.title: AEW All In 2026 match card, preview and predictions
item.description: Kenny Omega defends the AEW World Championship against Will Ospreay in the main event at Wembley Stadium, headlining a stacked AEW All In card.
item.content:encoded:
All Elite Wrestling (AEW) will hold its biggest event of the year at Wembley Stadium in London on Sunday.

All In has proven to be a showcase of some of the pro wrestling’s best. This year will be no different with championship matches up and down the card, including the AEW World Championship being on the line between Kenny Omega and Will Ospreay.

All In has also featured some surprises in the past with massive returns and debuts that have shaped the AEW roster.

Read below for a list of the match card, a preview and predictions for how All In will shake out.

COMPLETE PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE ON OUTKICK

==

A major trios match will kick off the two-hour All In Buy In and bleed into the first few minutes of All In. Adam Page and Brodido, the Bang Bang Gang, The Conglomeration, the Death Riders, The Demand and The Dogs will compete for the AEW World Trios Championship. But there is a wildcard entrant in this match. It could be anyone or it could be who we’re all expecting it to be. All In has been full of surprises in recent years. Let’s get another one in to start the show off with a bang.

Prediction: Adam Page and Brodido retain the trios title despite the chaos that will ensue.

==

Kyle Fletcher, Konosuke Takeshita and Kazuchika Okada may be three of the best professional wrestlers in the world. Their rivalry began after Takeshita defeated Okada for the AEW International Championship at Double or Nothing. Fletcher returned and turned on Takeshita. Weeks later, Fletcher won the title at Dynamite: Spring Breakin’ and turned the title picture on its head. Now, the three men will meet at All In. And while it may seem like Fletcher and Okada are on the same page, with the title on the line, it’ll be every man for himself.

Prediction: Kyle Fletcher, somehow, pulls it out and retains the title.

==

Kevin Knight has been the TNT champion for more than 135 days after winning a 10-man Casino Gauntlet match in Vancouver back in April. He’s gone from a fan favorite to the most hated after he turned on "Speedball" Mike Bailey and aligned himself, loosely, with the Don Callis Family. He’s been one of the top stars on the AEW roster since then but may have feuded with the wrong guy in Darby Allin. The challenger has proven that he’s willing to go above and beyond to win any match – even without gold on the line. Allin has been back in the fray for some gold since losing his AEW world title at Double or Nothing to MJF. As he’s dealt with Knight’s mind games, Allin has still shown he’s not willing to go down easy. This will be a big matchup.

Prediction: Darby Allin ends Knight’s title reign.

==

Megan Bayne and Lena Kross, the Divine Dominion have been at the top of the AEW women’s tag team division since March and have dispatched every opponent who have come their way. The Brawling Birds, Alex Windsor and Jamie Hayter, have been two women who have not backed down from challenging Bayne and Kross. The Brawling Birds have their home country behind them in this match and the momentum may carry over for them to get the win.

Prediction: The Brawling Birds take home the gold.

==

It has been a long and grueling Continental Challenge Cup and the finals will see continental champion Jon Moxley defend his title against Nigel McGuiness. Moxley is back on the All In card after losing the AEW World Championship to Adam Page last year. Moxley is looking for his own personal redemption and it may come at the expense of Nigel McGuiness, who is already battling an injury. McGuiness’ in-ring appearances have been few and far between but getting back in shape to make it through to the end is an accomplishment in and of itself. I don’t think Moxley can afford to lose this match.

Prediction: Moxley retains the AEW Continental Championship.

==

The men’s Casino Gauntlet match will have a title shot waiting for the winner. The match has seen its own share of surprises in the past and this one may not be different. We already know who the initial entrants are: Andrade El Idolo, MJF, Tommaso Ciampa, Mark Davis and Chris Jericho. Nobody knows who else is going to be in this match, which could make for some wild in-ring action. MJF has the edge after winning this match last year at All In. Will he be able to pull it off again or is his focus too much on AEW national champion Andrade?

Prediction: It’s a wild one. Somehow, Chris Jericho sneaks away with the victory.

==

Mercedes Moné has been lusting to get back on top of the AEW women’s division since her return to the ring earlier this year. She won the Owen Hart Foundation Women’s Tournament to earn a shot at the AEW Women’s World Championship. After Willow Nightingale defeated Thekla at Redemption, the match at All In became more about the history between Moné and Nightingale than just the championship. Nightingale was the fourth-ever AEW TBS champion and held the belt for 35 days before Moné ended her first reign. Moné held that title for 584 days before Nightingale finally got her revenge. Nightingale was forced to give up her title due to an injury but made her way back to capture the AEW Women’s World Championship. Now, Moné is on her radar again and apparently delivered an on-screen hand injury to Nightingale on the final "Dynamite" before All In.

Prediction: Mercedes Moné picks up the title win.

==

The temps between the teams of Christian Cage and Adam Copeland and Matt and Nick Jackson have turned up ever since they teamed up at Grand Slam Mexico. Things between the teams got even more chaotic on "Dynamite" as Copeland was the last one standing when they butted heads. The AEW world tag titles have meant the world to have for Cope and Cage. But the Young Bucks have been a dominant force in tag team wrestling for years. It’s a fairly important matchup for the wrestling industry and it will be a treat to see these four men in the ring, going up against each other, at the same time.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

Prediction: Cope and Cage retain in a great tag match.

==

It’s the match everyone is waiting for: Kenny Omega vs. Will Ospreay for the AEW World Championship. I don’t have to write too much on their history. Anyone who has ever watched pro wrestling knows the epic matches they put on in New Japan – some of the best matches in wrestling history. Both competitors are a little older now, and a little wiser. Omega is on top of the division as the champion after beating MJF at Spring Breakin’. Ospreay won the Owen Hart Foundation Men’s Tournament to earn the title shot, which everyone initially thought was going to be against MJF. But now Ospreay has a chance to dethrone his "hero" in Omega and do it in the main event at Wembley Stadium in his home country. Ospreay has been clear that it has always been his dream to be the focal point at Wembley and now he can be that and more.

Prediction: It is Will Ospreay’s time. Ospreay wins in a massive main event.

==

AEW All In begins at 1 p.m. ET and can be purchased in the United States on HBO Max, Amazon Prime, DAZN, PPV.com, YouTube, DirecTV, Sling and Dish Network. The Buy In begins at 11 a.m. ET.

item.title: Trump confirms Pentagon plans for 25th anniversary of 9/11 attacks, disputes report on Ground Zero absence
item.description: President Donald Trump said he will be at the Pentagon. A White House official said Vice President JD Vance will travel to New York for the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Friday that he's going to be at the Pentagon to mark the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 terrorist attacks.

A reporter on Friday asked the president why he was not planning to be in New York for the somber occasion.

"Because I'm going to the Pentagon," Trump shouted to the press at Joint Base Andrews.

On Thursday, The New York Times reported that Trump was not planning to attend the ceremony at Ground Zero, where the Twin Towers came down, because he wouldn't be allowed to give a speech. The annual event has banned politicians from speaking since 2012.

I LOST MY WIFE ON 9/11. PLEASE LET THIS 25TH ANNIVERSARY BELONG TO THE FAMILIES

When asked about the Times report, a White House spokeswoman called Trump a "proud New Yorker."

"President Trump has spoken about his own experiences watching the horrific events of September 11, 2001. On the 25th anniversary of this tragic day, the President will remember those who were killed at the hands of evil terrorists, honor their loved ones, and pay tribute to the brave first responders who put their lives on the line to rescue their fellow Americans," White House principal deputy press secretary Anna Kelly said in a statement to Fox News.

"The vice president is still traveling to NYC and all three sites will be represented with administration officials in attendance," a White House official said, referring to the three Sept. 11 attack sites in Manhattan, at the Pentagon and near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, where United Airlines Flight 93 crashed.

After TMZ posted on X that Trump was "snubbing" the Ground Zero ceremony, White House communications director Steven Cheung fired back.

"FAKE NEWS," Cheung wrote.

Trump lambasted the reporter behind in the Times article, writing on Truth Social Friday that she "made up a story that on September 11th, I’m not going to the World Trade Center, in New York City, because they won’t let me make a speech, and I’m going to the Pentagon in D.C., because I’m a featured speaker."

"This is more Corrupt News, I’ve been to New York many times over the years, and no one ever speaks, it’s a 'solemn ceremony!'" Trump wrote in part.

Trump said, "I would love not to speak, because I’m speaking all the time, and this is a day to remember the victims, and their beautiful family members."

Last year, Trump also chose to speak at the Pentagon for the 24th anniversary of 9/11, though he traveled to New York City later in the day to attend a Yankees game.

JUDGE THROWS OUT KHALID SHEIKH MOHAMMED'S 9/11 CONFESSION IN ALREADY LONG WAIT FOR TRIAL

The last time he attended the Ground Zero ceremony was in 2024, when he was the Republican presidential nominee. He was there alongside then-President Joe Biden and his election rival, then-Vice President Kamala Harris.

Trump also did not attend the Ground Zero ceremony during his first term. He spoke at the Pentagon in 2017, then alternated in subsequent years between commemorations there and at the site in Pennsylvania.

Nearly 3,000 people were killed in the terrorist attacks on Sept. 11, 2001, when al-Qaeda hijackers crashed three commercial airliners into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon. Hijackers also seized United Airlines Flight 93, but passengers fought back before the plane crashed in Pennsylvania.

The 9/11 attacks, which remain the deadliest in the nation's history, prompted the invasion of Afghanistan and helped usher in the broader War on Terror, which later included the U.S.-led invasion of Iraq.

Fox News' Patrick Ward contributed to this report.

item.title: Pop star-turned-Dem candidate’s defense of graphic murder video resurfaces in key House race
item.description: Bobby Pulido defended Gerardo Ortiz's graphic music video depicting sexual violence, adding to controversies as he challenges Monica De La Cruz.
item.content:encoded:
In a 2016 interview, Latin Grammy Award-winning artist and Democratic congressional candidate Bobby Pulido defended a fellow singer against criticism for a graphic music video that depicted acts of sexual violence and murder.

In the video production of "Fuiste Mía" or "You were mine" by Gerardo Ortiz, a singer walks in on his girlfriend cheating on him. After shooting her lover, he then handcuffs her to a pole, blindfolds her, and gropes her before putting her in the trunk of his car and setting it on fire.

In response to backlash, Pulido defended Ortiz, calling the video a matter of artistic direction.

"I've made videos with suggestive images; some have stayed, others have been edited, and still others were never used. That's the decision of the artist and their team," Pulido said in response to public backlash against the production.

Pulido’s resurfaced response to the music video is the latest in a series of controversies he has tried to downplay as he pursues a seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in Texas’ 15th Congressional District — one of the country’s most competitive seats.

FORMER DISNEY TEEN STAR EXPOSES CHILLING WARNING SIGNS OF PREDATORY BEHAVIOR IN HOLLYWOOD

Pulido is best known for Tejano, or Mexican–Spanish folk-style, songs like "Desvelado" and "Se Murió de Amor," and received five nominations for a Latin Grammy Awards, winning Best Tejano Album in 2025 and 2022.

He filed to run for Congress in Texas’ 15th District, challenging Rep. Monica De La Cruz, R-Texas. A two-term incumbent, she last won election to the district in 2024 in a 57.1% to 42.9% victory over Democratic nominee Michelle Vallejo. 

Along the way, Pulido has drawn scrutiny for a resurfaced history of posting links to explicit websites on his personal X account — as well as for a social media post of what appeared to be him urinating on President Donald Trump’s Hollywood Walk of Fame star. Pulido has shrugged off criticism for both, stating in 2024 that it's "it’s impossible to have Twitter and not watch porn," and that he had only poured water on Trump’s star as a joke.

More notably, Pulido has also had to fend off criticisms of bringing a registered sex offender to a Texas middle school benefit concert in 2018.

DEM TIED TO CARTEL OPERATIVE SAYS 'WHITE NATIONALISTS' JOINING IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT TO 'HUNT DOWN PEOPLE'

In that case, Pulido denied knowledge of his associate’s status at the time and has dismissed coverage of it as a "nothing story," according to Axios.

Similarly, in his defense of Ortiz, Pulido downplayed the music video, arguing that viewers had become accustomed to increasingly graphic images.

"What happens when there's a [car] accident?" Pulido asked, comparing the music video to real-life instances of tragedy.

"Traffic doesn't flow because people slow down or even stop to see what happened; something similar happens with the regional Mexican genre when these kinds of incidents occur.

Pulido in the 2016 interview also noted that he didn't agree always with his fellow artists' depictions of women but said he believes everyone is entitled to an opinion.

When asked about the music video and Pulido's response to it, his campaign framed it as a distraction from other elements in the race, including controversy on the Republican side of the aisle.

"This is emblematic of national Republicans doing anything and everything to distract voters from what are very real — not based on a fictional video — child abuse accusations against Monica De La Cruz and her refusal to release the Epstein files after thousands of girls were trafficked and abused," a Pulido campaign spokesperson said.

De La Cruz's former husband, Johnny Hernández, accused her of verbally abusing his 14-year-old daughter from a previous relationship in 2021 divorce proceedings. Authorities did not press charges or open an investigation into the allegations.

"Monica De La Cruz knows she’s losing, so she’s deploying the RNC to do her dirty work and deliberately mischaracterized a decade-old Spanish-language interview, in which Bobby said he respects artists’ right to make their own music – a right that Republicans used to believe in but apparently don’t when it comes to their opponents," the campaign added.

DEM RIPPED FOR ‘DISGUSTING’ ABSENCE ON BILL TO PUNISH VIOLENT CRIMINALS AFTER GIRL STRANGLED IN GRISLY KILLING

At least one Republican onlooker is left unconvinced by the defense of the music video — and defenses of other past behaviors.

"Bobby Pulido has spent his entire adult life defending perverts and predators while lashing out at members of law enforcement who keep Texans safe. He is a truly sick individual who is morally rotten," Zach Kraft, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee (RNC), said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

Having cleared their respective primaries, Pulido and De La Cruz will face off in the state's general elections on Nov. 3.

item.title: Dolly Parton's path from Nashville newcomer to Billboard's No. 1 country music artist of all time
item.description: Dolly Parton gained national attention in 1964 on "The Porter Wagoner Show," later becoming a 10-time Grammy Award-winner and Academy Award nominee.
item.content:encoded:
Dolly Parton's career as an entertainer spanned roughly seven decades.

During that time, the legendary country music star cemented herself as an icon not only in the music industry, but also as a movie star and a philanthropist.

From getting her start on "The Porter Wagoner Show" in 1964 to multiple Academy Award nominations, Parton forged a path for herself in the industry and paved the way for female country singers who followed her.

DOLLY PARTON’S SIX-DECADE LOVE STORY WITH CARL DEAN BEGAN AT A LAUNDROMAT

Here are some of Parton's career highlights.

Parton moved to Nashville, Tennessee, in May 1964, the day after graduating from high school, to pursue a career in country music.

Three years later, she released her debut album, "Hello, I'm Dolly," in February 1967, which caught the attention of singer Porter Wagoner. He then invited Parton to join him on his TV show, "The Porter Wagoner Show," a few months later, in September 1967.

Parton's time on the show provided her with national attention and established her as a recording artist. Her duets with Wagoner, starting with "The Last Thing on My Mind," became major country hits. Their partnership also earned Parton her first Grammy nomination in 1970.

In addition to her duets with Wagoner, she also released many of her well-known songs during this era, including "Jolene," "Coat of Many Colors," "My Tennessee Mountain Home," "Just Because I'm a Woman" and many more.

After seven years on the show, Parton felt it was time to pursue a solo career, ultimately leaving the show in 1974.

Shortly after leaving the show, Parton released "Love Is Like a Butterfly," which quickly climbed to the top of the Billboard country charts.

She continued releasing hit after hit, including "Here You Come Again," off the album with the same name, which earned her first Grammy Award win in 1979.

She had 26 songs reach No. 1 on the Billboard country charts, including "The Bargain Store," "Heartbreaker," "Starting Over Again," "Tennessee Homesick Blues" and "Why'd You Come in Here Lookin' Like That."

In addition to her own music, Parton found success covering other artists' songs in her own style, including "Stairway to Heaven," "The House of the Rising Sun," "Shine" and others.

"Yes, and they loved it. Robert’s been out on tour, so he’s been doing a lot of interviews," she told Hot Press in 2002 about Led Zeppelin singer Robert Plant's reaction to her "Stairway to Heaven" cover. "And he seems to make mention of it a lot – I guess because people are asking him about it – and he says something different every time, but he seems to like it. He says he really likes what I did with it, and that makes me feel good."

Parton wrote one of her most well-known songs, "I Will Always Love You," in 1973 when she told Wagoner she wanted to leave the show and go solo.

When Wagoner responded negatively and all her efforts to get him to understand her reasoning fell on deaf ears, Parton thought she would put all her feelings into a song and play it for him to help him understand.

"I said, ‘Porter, sit down. I got something I need to sing to you,’" she told Howard Stern in 2023. "He was just sitting behind his desk and tears started rolling down. He said, ‘That’s just the best song you ever wrote, and you can go if I can produce the song.’"

The song was released in 1974 as part of her "Jolene" album, and climbed to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot Country Singles chart. It returned to No. 1 again in 1982 when Parton released a different version for "The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas."

Nearly two decades after the song's initial release, Whitney Houston's version reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart, where it stayed for 14 consecutive weeks.

Houston recorded an R&B ballad version of the song for the soundtrack to "The Bodyguard."

In addition to staying at the No. 1 spot for 14 weeks, it was Billboard's No. 1 song of 1993, went 19-times Platinum in the U.S., and won two Grammy Awards at the 1994 ceremony. This version of the song is also the highest-selling single written by a female artist.

"I almost wrecked, honest to god. I had to pull over to a Walgreens … and listen to the rest of it," Parton told Stern about hearing Houston's version for the first time. "I couldn’t believe my little country sad song could even be done like that … and it was just overwhelming. That was one of the greatest experiences I ever had in my entire life."

Two years after leaving "The Porter Wagoner Show," Parton started her own variety show called "Dolly!" in 1976.

The show aired 26 half-hour episodes and featured guest stars such as Kenny Rogers, Linda Ronstadt, Emmylou Harris, Anne Murray and many others.

Ten years after that show ended, she released a second variety show, "Dolly," in 1987.

The show aired 22 one-hour episodes from September 1987 to May 1988 and was a huge ratings success, featuring guests such as Oprah Winfrey, Bruce Willis and Loretta Lynn as well as Kermit the Frog and Miss Piggy.

In addition to Wagoner, Parton had several other significant collaborations throughout her career.

One of her most celebrated partnerships was with Kenny Rogers. The two first connected in 1983 when they recorded the hit song, "Islands In the Stream" together. The song was a massive crossover hit and spent two consecutive weeks at No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart and earned them a Grammy nomination.

The two later released a joint Christmas album in 1984, titled "Once Upon a Christmas," and a year later collaborated on "Real Love," which reached No. 1 on Billboard’s Hot Country Singles chart.

Nearly 30 years later, they released "You Can't Make Old Friends" in 2013, the title track of Rogers' album with the same name, earning them another Grammy nomination.

"It really made me very emotional," Parton told ABC News in September 2013 about the song. "Even when I was recording it I was tearful, and when I was listening to the demo it really just, you know, it certainly summed us up and our relationship. But it also is such a song of friendship of all kinds."

Parton also partnered with Emmylou Harris and Linda Ronstadt in 1987 to release their highly successful album, "Trio," which largely featured covers, except for "Wildflowers," which was written by Parton for the album.

The album reached No. 1 on Billboard's country albums chart and No. 6 on the Billboard 200 and earned the three artists a Grammy.

They followed it with "Trio II" in 1999, which featured a highly praised cover of Neil Young's song "After the Gold Rush," which earned them yet another Grammy.

In addition to these collaborations, Parton released songs with Brad Paisley, Vince Gill, Willie Nelson, Reba McEntire, Miley Cyrus and others.

After making a name for herself in the music world, she set her sights on movies.

Parton made her feature film debut in the 1980 classic comedy "9 to 5," which also starred Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin. Tomlin, Fonda and Parton played a trio of secretaries who took revenge on their sexist boss by kidnapping him and enacting changes in the workplace in his name.

The movie was an instant classic, earning Parton three Golden Globe nominations and an Oscar nomination for best original song for the song she wrote for the film, "9 to 5."

Two years later, Parton made a splash with a second critically-acclaimed role in the film "The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas," playing Miss Mona, a madam at the Chicken Ranch, a long-running Texas brothel.

Her role in the film earned her another Golden Globe nomination.

She then starred in the 1989 movie "Steel Magnolias," alongside Hollywood heavy-hitters Sally Field, Shirley MacLaine, Daryl Hannah, Olympia Dukakis and Julia Roberts. 

Together they portrayed a group of Southern women who banded together during life's good and hard moments, with Parton in particular playing a hair stylist.

"I totally related to her. She's not different from me at all, and it wasn't hard for me to play a Southern girl with a Southern accent," she told "Today" in 1989. "And it's not foreign to me, like you said in your intro, for me to do hair, 'cause I grew up doing my sister's hair, my friends' hair – I started cutting and bleaching in a salon on my own at 15 years old and I loved it."

Throughout her career, she also appeared in the films "Rhinestone," "Straight Talk," "The Beverly Hillbillies," "Miss Congeniality 2: Armed and Fabulous," "Joyful Noise" and others, including appearing on three episodes of "Hannah Montana."

Parton received many accolades during her roughly seven decades in the entertainment industry.

Since releasing her first album in 1967, Parton has received a total of 55 Grammy Award nominations, resulting in 10 wins. Her first win came in 1979 in the female country vocal performance for her song "Here You Come Again."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

She later won awards for "9 to 5," "Trio," "The Grass Is Blue," "Shine" and other projects, with her final nomination coming in 2025 for best audiobook narration and storytelling recording for her memoir, "Behind The Seams: My Life In Rhinestones."

Her music was also celebrated in the film world, with two Academy Award nominations for best original song. The first came in 1981 for her song, "9 to 5," and the second in 2006 for the song, "Travelin' Thru," featured in the movie, "Transamerica."

Parton received six Golden Globe nominations over her career, including three connected to "9 to 5" and one for her performance in "The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas." She also won an Emmy Award for outstanding television movie as an executive producer of "Christmas on the Square."

She also won 10 CMA Awards out of 45 nominations, including entertainer of the year in 1978, five ACM Awards and seven CMT Awards.

Parton was honored in other ways, in addition to the many awards she accumulated throughout her career.

In 1984, the singer received her star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame, and was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1999 and the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2001.

She later received a Kennedy Center Honor in 2006, recognizing her contributions to American culture.

In 2022, Parton was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame. Two years later, Billboard named Parton the No. 1 country music artist of all time.

"People usually [say] ‘Dolly rocks’ or ‘you rock’ or ‘you’re a rock star.’ I thought they just meant that I was cool, and I took that as a great compliment," she told Billboard in February 2022 about the induction. "But now I’m going to have to take it literally!"

Apart from her work as an entertainer, Parton was also known for her philanthropy.

She started the Imagination Library in 1995, which sends free books to children around the world from birth to age five, no matter their families' economic status. She was inspired to create the program by her father, who never learned to read or write.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

According to the organization's website, over three million kids have registered and over 330 million books have been gifted since the program started.

"When I was growing up in the hills of East Tennessee, I knew my dreams would come true. I know there are children in your community with their own dreams," Parton said in a statement on the website. "They dream of becoming a doctor or an inventor or a minister. Who knows, maybe there is a little girl whose dream is to be a writer and singer. The seeds of these dreams are often found in books and the seeds you help plant in your community can grow across the world."

Parton showed off her business knowledge when she opened her own theme park called Dollywood in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee, in 1986.

PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

Not only was the theme park popular, drawing about four million visitors annually, it also provided job opportunities for thousands of people in the area, proving Parton was all about giving back to her community.

"The Smokies – and the wonderful people who work here – are what make Dollywood so different than many of the other theme parks around the world," she told National Geographic in January 2024, per People. "We’re right on the front porch of the most-visited national park in the country, so we take what God gave us and use it to dream up the big dreams we want our guests to experience while they are here riding rides and making memories."

In addition to her own chart-toppers, Parton wrote many songs for other artists which were also big hits.

Included in the list are "Kentucky Gambler," which she wrote for Merle Haggard and became a No. 1 country hit in 1975, and "Put It Off Until Tomorrow" for Bill Phillips, which became a top 10 country hit.

She also wrote "Waltz Me to Heaven" for Waylon Jennings, "The Stranger" for Kenny Rogers," "I'm In No Condition" for Hank Williams Jr., "Love, You’re So Beautiful Tonight" for Willie Nelson and "There'll Always Be Music" for Tina Turner.

These are far from all the songs she wrote, as it is reported that Parton had a catalog of over 3,000 songs penned by her.

item.title: BROADCAST BIAS: Dolly Parton taught the world the way to be universally beloved
item.description: Dolly Parton navigated tough interviews from Barbara Walters to political questions about Trump while building an ironclad legacy of kindness.
item.content:encoded:
When the news broke that Dolly Parton had died at age 80, the networks exploded in tributes and primetime specials about her career in music and acting and her plethora of good works. Everyone remarked on how rare it was that someone could be universally beloved. How could that be done?

Some of the answer to that is simple: Be kind to everyone. Be generous in spirit and with your wealth. One crucial thing, especially in the last 10 years, is to steer entirely clear of politics, if such a thing is possible. The media has tried to shame entertainers who refuse to speak on politics. Dolly brought her aura of celebrity and philanthropy in a way that she could escape the shaming attempts.

But she perfected the formula a long time ago, ingratiating herself to a broad audience. One of the old TV clips making the rounds was a 1977 interview on ABC with Barbara Walters, who asked questions that could come across as offensive, even hostile. "Dolly, where I come from, would I have called you a hillbilly?" She hinted that parts of her body might be artificial: "Is it all you?"

DOLLY PARTON'S LIFE IN HER OWN WORDS: FROM SMOKY MOUNTAINS POVERTY TO COUNTRY MUSIC IMMORTALITY

Then, about her appearance in general, Walters pressed: "You don't have to look like this. You're very beautiful. You don't have to wear the blonde wigs. You don't have to wear the extreme clothes, right? ... Do you ever feel that you're a joke that people make fun of you?"

Dolly never took offense. Walters had a habit of trying to ask questions the audience at home might be thinking, so these questions were a chance to address them. Perhaps the roughest question was about how she didn’t see much of her husband Carl Dean on the road, so Walters asked if the love was real, and, "Why have a husband away someplace to see six weeks a year?"

STEVE DOOCY: THE DOLLY PARTON I SAW WHEN THE CAMERAS STOPPED ROLLING

Walters was married four times to three different men, so maybe she was reflecting on her own nature, if not Dolly’s, who was married to her husband for almost 60 years, until he died last year.

In 2018, Dolly talked to ABC correspondent David Wright, and he brought up the plot of the movie "9 to 5" and then tried to relate that to President Donald Trump: "The sexist, egotistical, lying, hypocritical bigot portrayed so effectively in that movie by actor Dabney Coleman hasn’t exactly disappeared from the culture. We have a president of the United States who said the things on that bus." (That would be the audio that leaked in 2016 where Trump mused to "Access Hollywood" host Billy Bush about grabbing women.)

Dolly rolled out her usual answer: "I'm not addressing that. I do not get into that. Of course, I have my opinion about everybody and everything. But I learned a long time ago, keep your damn mouth shut if you want to stay in show business. I'm not in politics. I am an entertainer." The ABC correspondent whined, "And yet you’re also a role model." She replied: "Yes, I am. That's why I don't talk about people."

After her passing, NBC touted that it had conducted over 50 interviews with Dolly on "Today," and noted that Robert Goldblatt, who helped Dolly create the Broadway musical version of "9 to 5," became the chairman of NBC Entertainment, and they partnered in two "Coat of Many Colors" movies about Dolly’s childhood, in 2015 and in 2016.

DOLLY PARTON OFFERED TO TRY EXPERIMENTAL DRUGS IF ‘NO HOPE’ FOR CANCER BATTLE TO HELP OTHERS, SISTER SAYS

It was her father’s inability to read and write that spurred Dolly to create her most celebrated charity, the Imagination Library, in 1995. They have distributed over 300 million books to children to promote literacy. That’s a good cause, no matter what your politics might be.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Her other philanthropic works, from funding disaster relief after local wildfires in Tennessee to development of the COVID-19 vaccine, built that ironclad positive reputation. But as you can tell from all of this week’s outpouring of testimony from famous and not-famous people about her kindness and supportive nature, she also built her reputation, day by day, in many interactions with people who were just astonished to be in her presence. To remain humble after all her fame and fortune defies the stereotype of self-obsessed celebrities.

To people who have been granted so much, it’s a challenge to give back, and Dolly Parton seemed to return every demand on her attention with patience and grace. It’s no wonder everyone marvels at her example.

Mica’s family discusses the alleged hospitalization in "Death of the Pastor’s Wife," a three-part true-crime series that premiered Wednesday on Netflix. The documentary delves into her life, marriage and April 2024 death, which authorities ruled a suicide.

item.title: ‘Quiet quitting’ in marriage: The subtle signs a spouse has emotionally checked out
item.description: Licensed therapist Lisa Brookes Kift outlines how "quiet quitting" erodes marriages, and why the absence of arguing may signal emotional detachment.
item.content:encoded:
"Quiet quitting," a workplace term for doing only the minimum required, has also been used to describe a pattern in some marriages.

In relationships, the informal term refers to spouses who remain together while reducing their emotional effort, communication or involvement in the relationship.

Couples may continue managing day-to-day responsibilities, such as household tasks and parenting, even as one partner becomes emotionally and physically disengaged, relationship experts say.

‘NO CONTACT’ ON THE RISE: NEARLY 2 IN 5 AMERICANS CUT TIES WITH LOVED ONES

Discussion of the term has gained traction on social media, with users sharing videos and posts about remaining in a marriage while feeling checked out.

Licensed marriage and family therapist Lisa Brookes Kift, of Marin Therapy and Counseling in California, told Fox News Digital that a noticeable absence of friction can be an early warning sign.

"It’s a myth that an absence of arguing in a relationship automatically means the relationship is healthy," Kift said. "Many are conflict-avoidant and rather than address their feelings, opt to sweep them under the rug, which over the long term erodes the foundation of emotional safety."

Kift said a person’s attachment style — patterns of seeking closeness and support in relationships — can influence how they respond to marital distress.

CUT OFF BY YOUR ADULT CHILD? PSYCHOLOGY RESEARCHER REVEALS WHAT PARENTS SHOULD DO NEXT

"An avoidant style may be more able to stay in their own lane — on their own island — to ride it out, because they are most comfortable resourcing in themselves," she said.

Those with a more secure attachment style are less likely to stay in that dynamic, as they may be more inclined to give a partner the benefit of the doubt and believe problems can be worked through, the expert noted.

These patterns can be shaped, in part, by early experiences involving trust, worthiness and whether a person’s emotional needs were met, according to Kift.

"What did they learn about whether their needs would be met? Whether the most important people to them could be trusted? That they were lovable for who they were and not what they did?" Kift asked.

When adult relationships appear to repeat those early disappointments, partners can lose hope, she added.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

"I’ve seen quite a few people in my therapy practice who have taken this stance, where there have been failed attempts to get emotional and other needs met, leading to hopelessness," Kift said.

Kift identified several early signs that a partner may be becoming emotionally disengaged.

Left unaddressed, the relationship could shift into what journalist Monica Corcoran Harel described on Oprah’s podcast as "parallel play" — a reference to toddlers playing side by side without meaningfully engaging with one another.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Repairing a marriage requires both partners to re-engage, Kift said, which can be difficult once one spouse has become deeply emotionally detached.

"If one has fully checked out, they will not be open to repair," she said, adding that hypervigilance — remaining on guard for hurt or disappointment — can make it difficult for a person to recognize positive changes in their partner.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

For couples willing to work on the relationship, Kift suggests starting with a conversation that feels safe and communicates care.

As one example, she suggested saying: "I know it may not have looked like it, but you and our marriage are very important to me. Can we find a time to sit down and talk?"

item.title: NFL restarts social justice messaging while battling domestic abuse, drunk driving and prostitution arrests
item.description: The NFL will bring back "Stop Hate" and "End Racism" end zone stencils for 2026 while facing a wave of player arrests and conduct investigations.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL will again during the 2026 season stencil its end zones and adorn helmets with "Stop Hate" or "End Racism" as part of its social justice messaging even as the league is inundated in arrests, court dates and personal conduct policy investigations having to do with criminal justice.

The league wants to advance the message that every person deserves equal economic, political, and social rights, regardless of their background. And that's good.

But it is not making any similar messaging push for stopping men getting physical with women, people driving under the influence or stopping human trafficking – even after one of its owners, Jed York of the San Francisco 49ers, got arrested by a human trafficking task force in Ohio in a prostitution sting.

49ERS OWNER JED YORK ARRESTED FOR 'ENGAGING IN PROSTITUTION' IN OHIO, PLEADS NO CONTEST TO LESSER CHARGES

So the league is making social justice a priority while criminal justice needs addressing within its ranks.

The return of the social justice push for 2026 was first reported by Front Office Sports. A league spokesman told OutKick that clubs will again have the opportunity to select their preferred end zone stencil messaging.

The available options for 2026 for the clubs are the same as last year – "Choose Love," "Inspire Change," "End Racism" and "Stop Hate."

Clubs can also use "Never Forget" on Week 1, which is in memoriam of the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks.

Players can also again select from the four messages for their helmet decals throughout the season.

Here's a thought: Any club not picking "Never Forget" on Week 1 is failing, regardless of what they pick the remainder of the season.

Despite the NFL's social justice messaging on its fields and player helmets the rest of this year and every year since 2020, the FBI recorded a 51% increase in bias-motivated incidents from 2020 to 2024.

The Anti-Defamation League recorded 2,024 antisemitic incidents in 2020, but by 2024 that number had risen to 9,354 — a more than fourfold increase.

In 2020, the FBI reported 7,759 hate crimes. That number was at 10,881 in 2025.

These rising statistics amid the NFL's social justice campaign is obviously not the league's fault, but it does raise the question whether its audience is the proper target. And if the league can continue a campaign that isn't necessarily stopping hate or racism, why can't it also take on the criminal problems that some of its own employees apparently have?

NFL EMPLOYEES' TROUBLING DRIVING INCIDENTS MOUNT, COSTING JOBS AND PUTTING OTHERS AT RISK

The two campaigns wouldn't have to be mutually exclusive.

The NFL could stencil its end zones with "Stop drinking and driving" just as it will with one of the four options presented to teams for most of the season.

The league could perhaps benefit from such messaging in its stadiums and on its helmets because DUI arrests or other traffic incidents involving NFL people are not uncommon.

Consider:

The Washington Commanders fired tight end coach Ben Steele on the eve of training camp following a DWI arrest in June.

Defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander was suspended by the Minnesota Vikings after he pleaded guilty to third-degree DWI. 

The Los Angeles Chargers released guard Ben Cleveland after he was arrested on charges of speeding and driving with a limited permit. That arrest came roughly one-and-a-half-years removed from Cleveland being arrested for DUI.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and current CBS NFL analyst Tony Romo was arrested in Wisconsin for OWI, which is Operating While Intoxicated, unsafe passing, open intoxicants and refusing a breathalyzer. A hearing is scheduled for Sept. 21.

The NFL could also benefit from messaging that addresses domestic violence. The league has seen a not insignificant number of its players or others involved in domestic incidents this year.

Just this week, Packers running back Josh Jacobs was charged with battery and one other misdemeanor count in an incident allegedly involving his ex-girlfriend.

Falcons edge rusher James Pearce was suspended for the first eight games of the season after he was embroiled in a domestic incident and arrested in February.

NFL PUTS 'INSPIRE CHANGE' AND 'CHOOSE LOVE' ON FIELDS BUT NOT SO AGGRESSIVE ABOUT ITS DOMESTIC ABUSE ISSUES

Ravens receiver Rashod Bateman, Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper, Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson, and free agent receiver Tyreek Hill, also have run afoul of police or courts or both because of domestic issues this year.

So, here's an end zone stencil idea the NFL should consider: "Tackle men but don't touch women."
